---
title: "STACK questions with AI Feedback"
subtitle: "Interactive practice on Quarto teaching pages"
---

Bring selected Moodle STACK questions to a teaching website. Learners practise
in their browser, see how their answers are interpreted, and can request
guided **AI Feedback** alongside the question's mathematical grading. The
exported XML, scoring rules and author tests remain available for inspection.

**Quarto** turns plain-text teaching material into web pages. STACK SymPy adds
interactive question cards to those pages for publication as a static site.

## For teachers

### Try a question {#try-a-question}

Expand and collect the polynomial below. An equivalent factored answer earns
partial credit. Press **Validate answers** to inspect your expression, then
**Check answer** to grade it. Change the variant to try fresh coefficients.
The **AI Feedback** panel offers guided hints and explanations; it does not
replace the question's scoring. Review controls let authors replay the
question's own tests.

```{.stack-question}
#| file: questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| variants: 3
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
```

[Download this STACK XML](questions/polynomial-expansion.xml) ·
[Try more questions](examples.qmd)

### What is supported? {#what-is-supported}

| Teaching task | What to try next |
|---|---|
| Equivalent algebra or a required written form | [Rational and form-sensitive questions](examples.qmd#algebraic-equivalence-and-written-form) |
| A measured number with tolerance or reported decimal places | [Numerical questions](examples.qmd#numerical-answers-and-precision) |
| Polynomial equations or Boolean propositions | [Equations and logic](examples.qmd#equations-and-logic) |
| Ordered lists, sets and nested finite collections | [Collection questions](examples.qmd#collections) |
| A particular matrix, any basis, or a matrix meeting conditions | [Matrix examples](examples.qmd#matrix-conditions) and [choosing an answer test](docs/python-checker-api.qmd#choose-the-mathematical-test) |
| Another authored condition, such as positive definiteness | [Live SPD question](examples.qmd#symmetric-positive-definite-matrix) and its [authoring walkthrough](docs/python-checker-api.qmd#author-the-spd-checker) |

These activities cover a defined part of STACK. The [authoring guide](docs/authoring.qmd#what-the-adapter-checks) maps teaching tasks to supported tests; its [developer reference](docs/authoring.qmd#for-developers) records precise input, expression and grading limits.
The [question corpus](corpus.qmd) shows which unchanged imports currently run
and which need author attention.

### Use your own question {#use-your-own-question}

1. Export a supported question from Moodle as STACK XML.
2. Add STACK SymPy to a Quarto project and embed the named question in a page.
3. Run its author tests, render the site and inspect an alternate correct and
   an incorrect answer before publishing.

The [authoring guide](docs/authoring.qmd) gives the installation steps,
embedding example and AI Feedback setup. For a question asking for any basis
or any matrix with a chosen property, start with [Python answer
tests](docs/python-checker-api.qmd). A native Moodle STACK version of a
Python-only question needs equivalent Maxima checks.

## For developers

### Explore the port {#explore-the-port}

The existing STACK answer-test families implemented here are `AlgEquiv`,
`Sets`, `SameType`, `EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac`, `LowestTerms`,
`NumAbsolute`, `NumRelative` and `NumDecPlaces`. The Python-only `IsBasis`,
`MatrixProperty` and author-supplied `PythonChecker` tests add tasks such as
alternate bases and matrix conditions without changing those native test
names. Ordinary response trees still control scores and feedback.

- [Python answer-test guide](docs/python-checker-api.qmd): matrix choices,
  teacher values, callback contract and complete SPD example.
- [STACK compliance](compliance/): comparisons with upstream answer-test cases.
- [Port regressions](compliance/port-regressions.html): focused checks for
  mathematical behavior discovered during the port.
- [Source and development guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#readme):
  setup and implementation notes.
